definition: The study of how to automatically learn useful features or representations of data, rather than relying on hand-engineered features.
details: Representation learning is a core theme underlying deep learning's success, since neural networks trained on large datasets automatically discover representations that are often more effective than manually designed features.

explainer.lead: It is the automatic discovery of useful features from data instead of hand-designing them. It matters because learned representations from large datasets often beat engineered features and underpin deep learning's gains.

tiers.eli5: Instead of being told to measure height, width and colour by hand, the system works out for itself which measurements are worth making.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train networks on large data so intermediate layers serve as reusable features for downstream tasks, often via pretraining then fine-tuning. A pitfall is that the learned representation encodes the biases and distribution of the pretraining data, which may not transfer.
tiers.paperLevel: Learning a mapping from raw inputs to a feature space such that a simple downstream model on those features performs well; success is measured by transfer to held-out tasks. There is no general guarantee that features useful for one task transfer to another.

explainer.example: A network pretrained on millions of images produces embeddings that a linear classifier can use to separate new categories with only a few labelled examples.
